mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior 3 months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% over the past 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar rising-rate regimes, or the 3-month FEDFUNDS change is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, wage growth accelerates and consumer confidence improves, both of which are associated with stronger corporate earnings expectations and higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In 5-year windows where unemployment <5% for >3 months, 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during high-unemployment periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (PCE) relative to GDP in the prior month indicates excess demand, which raises price pressures and corporate profit expectations, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth rate > 0.5% while GDPC1 > 2% of GDP
failure_condition: During periods of high inflation, the 20-day forward return does not outperform a risk-free rate proxy (e.g., 3-month Treasury bill yield).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production index above 105 signals robust manufacturing momentum that, when sustained for two months, lowers real interest rates via monetary accommodation, resulting in positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over 12 months with INDPRO > 105, 20-day forward returns are negative on average.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month change in FEDFUNDS turns positive after two consecutive months of negative changes, it signals a shift from contractionary to neutral policy, which supports equity valuations and yields positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS month-over-month crosses from negative to positive over a 3-month window
failure_condition: In 10 such policy normalization events, 5-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 6% for three months increases labor market participation and reduces labor cost pressures for firms, which raises earnings growth forecasts and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 6.0% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During periods of falling UNRATE < 6% for >3 months, 60-day forward returns are flat or negative.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales ( proxy: HOUST ) above 2,000 units indicate resilient consumer demand, which accelerates corporate investment and supports positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: In 12 such demand expansion events, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during baseline periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO < 90) followed by a two-month recovery suggests cyclical soft landing, reducing supply-side risks and prompting positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 90 then rises for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 8 such recovery episodes, 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1).
